items.title: Direct revalidation is not atomically bound to mutation
items.statement: OP-006 permits mutation after direct revalidation but does not require the revalidated version, lease, or source event to remain current through mutation commit. A projection can become stale again between the check and the write.

evidence.exact_quote: - Stale, degraded, and unavailable projections disable mutation unless the owner surface performs direct revalidation.

items.impact: A mutation may execute against superseded authority or state even though the UI just revalidated.
items.builder_discretion: Define an atomic compare-and-commit token, lease, or version precondition and a deterministic conflict result.

items.title: Wait recovery has no missing-record or offline branch
items.statement: The timeout card is required to route through a stored episode or receipt, but behavior is unspecified when storage is unavailable, the record was pruned, the reference is corrupt, or connectivity is lost during recovery.

evidence.exact_quote: - Wait and timeout cards show canonical retained timeout_class and route recovery through stored blocked episodes or receipts.

items.impact: Users can be offered a recovery route that cannot resolve or that silently points at incomplete state.
items.builder_discretion: Specify explicit unavailable, missing, corrupt, and retry-later outcomes without synthesizing a new failure identity.

items.title: Projection lineage lacks retention and disclosure boundaries
items.statement: The required source_event_ref and timestamps have no retention, redaction, project-isolation, or deletion contract even though they can expose execution lineage through mutation-capable projections.

evidence.exact_quote: - Mutation-capable projections carry projection_state, last_observed_at, source_event_ref, and revalidation_route.

items.impact: Lineage may outlive its project or be exposed to unauthorized callers.
items.builder_discretion: Define access control, redaction, retention, and tombstone behavior for projection lineage.

items.title: OP-006 is classified non-GUI despite mandatory card display
items.statement: The unit declares gui_related false while prescribing timeout-card display and mutation disabling. This classification can exclude required stale, degraded, unavailable, and timeout truth from GUI-focused compilation or validation.

evidence.exact_quote: gui_related: false
- Wait and timeout cards show canonical retained timeout_class and route recovery through stored blocked episodes or receipts.

items.impact: A GUI implementation can omit or misrepresent the safety state while still satisfying the unit classification.
items.builder_discretion: Reclassify or split the display and mutation-control portion into a GUI-related PlanUnit.

items.title: Stale observation cannot fabricate terminal outcome
items.statement: OP-006 explicitly prevents a stale observation from being interpreted as skipped or failed, preserving the distinction between observation quality and canonical execution outcome.

evidence.exact_quote: - "Do not infer skipped/failed from stale observation alone."

items.title: Object-first routes lack authorization and invalid-target semantics
items.statement: OP-007 defines route identity but not the result for unauthorized, deleted, moved, malformed, cross-project, or version-incompatible objects and filters. Stable IDs alone do not establish caller authority.

evidence.exact_quote: Search, command-palette, drill-down, and cross-tab deep links route by stable object identity, focused run context, destination tab, selected object id, optional filters, and inspector detail targets.

items.impact: Crafted or stale deep links can disclose existence, resolve in the wrong scope, or render a misleading target.
items.builder_discretion: Validate and authorize every route component at resolution time and define not-found, forbidden, gone, and invalid-route results.

items.title: Focused-run changes can race route resolution
items.statement: The focused_run_id contract does not specify whether a route snapshots focus, follows a later focus change, cancels in-flight resolution, or rejects a result that returns for the prior run. Offline reopening of a deep link is also undefined.

evidence.exact_quote: - Deep links stay coherent on focused_run_id and focus_mode rather than jumping to active_run_id implicitly.

items.impact: Late route results can show data from a run that is no longer focused or fail without an honest offline state.
items.builder_discretion: Bind resolution to a focus generation and define cancel, stale-result, and offline behavior.

items.title: Cross-run name collision is explicitly rejected
items.statement: OP-007 directly forbids collapsing similarly named objects across unrelated runs, providing an important route-integrity invariant.

evidence.exact_quote: - "Do not collapse similarly named seams, packages, nodes, or work packages across unrelated runs."

items.title: Notification escalation and ownership are not a state machine
items.statement: Severity, persistence, quieting, dismissal, reassignment, acknowledgment, duplicate events, and multiple simultaneous blocked owners have no ordered transition or conflict rules. The meaning and authority of a primary owner are not defined.

evidence.exact_quote: Notifications, attention rows, blocked-owner summaries, escalation levels, quieting behavior, and surface routing are determined by severity, execution impact, blocked owner, persistence, and projection trust.
- Blocked-owner summaries identify a primary blocked owner or attention owner.

items.impact: Concurrent updates can select the wrong owner, regress severity, or let a presentation action appear to resolve canonical work.
items.builder_discretion: Specify event ordering, deduplication, escalation/de-escalation, owner tie-breaking, reassignment, acknowledgment, and actor permissions.

items.title: Notification surfaces omit scale and accessible localized semantics
items.statement: The active/history split has no pagination, retention, coalescing, rate, overflow, or backpressure limits. Severity markers and badges have no non-color semantics, announcement order, focus behavior, or localization contract for labels and time-sensitive text.

evidence.exact_quote: - History receives chronological notifications while Progress and Dashboard show active warnings, attention, blocked states, severity markers, and badges.

items.impact: Large or bursty histories can become unusable, and critical state can be inaccessible or mistranslated.
items.builder_discretion: Define bounded history behavior, coalescing without loss of canonical episodes, semantic labels, live-region rules, and locale-safe copy.

items.title: Presentation quieting cannot erase canonical blockage
items.statement: OP-008 explicitly retains canonical blocked episodes across quieting and dismissal, protecting canonical state from presentation-only controls.

evidence.exact_quote: - "Quiet windows must never suppress canonical blocked episodes."
- "Dismissed presentation must not clear canonical blocked episodes that remain active."

items.title: Durable project and account records lack lifecycle contracts
items.statement: OP-009 calls records durable and project-scoped but omits stable record IDs, schema/version fields, creation/update ordering, retention, deletion, export, redaction, project deletion, and authorization rules.

evidence.exact_quote: Project summary, project attention item, account pressure episode, and account switch event records remain durable, project-scoped, and split between current-state and historical-state facts.

items.impact: Account-pressure and switch lineage can leak across projects, become undeletable, or lose interpretability after schema change.
items.builder_discretion: Define identities, versioning, tenant/project access, retention, deletion/tombstone, redaction, and export semantics.

items.title: Current and historical account facts have no concurrent ordering rule
items.statement: Splitting pressure cause, switch outcome, and history does not define an atomic transaction or reconciliation rule when two switches race, a switch partially succeeds, or history commits without the current projection.

evidence.exact_quote: - account_switch_reason is split into pressure cause, switch outcome, and historical lineage.

items.impact: Current account state and historical lineage can disagree or duplicate events after retry.
items.builder_discretion: Specify idempotency, sequence/version ordering, transactional boundaries, reconciliation, and retry behavior.

items.title: OP-009 GUI classification excludes user-visible projection disclosures
items.statement: The unit is marked non-GUI even though its acceptance criteria require project summaries and attention items to carry projection-trust disclosure for consumption across surfaces.

evidence.exact_quote: gui_related: false
- project_attention_item carries a primary route payload and projection-trust disclosure consumable across surfaces.

items.impact: User-facing surfaces can omit freshness disclosure while the non-GUI unit appears satisfied.
items.builder_discretion: Split or reclassify the cross-surface disclosure requirement as GUI-related.

items.title: Promotion revocation and reopen lack a legal transition model
items.statement: The canonical text requires revocation or reopen lineage, but acceptance criteria do not define legal source states, terminal precedence, downstream invalidation, partial rollback, idempotency, or whether a superseded decision can be reopened.

evidence.exact_quote: Promotion classes, review records, gate facts, evidence expectations, decision outcomes, and revocation or reopen lineage remain explicit package, seam, lane, and governance data.

items.impact: A revoked or reopened promotion can leave downstream package, seam, or governance state falsely promoted.
items.builder_discretion: Define the state graph, causal revision IDs, invalidation fan-out, rollback/recovery, and idempotent replay.

items.title: Reviewer identity is recorded but not authorized or verified
items.statement: The record preserves effective reviewer identity and evidence links but does not define who may review, decide, revoke, or reopen; separation of duties; delegated identity; signature/tamper verification; or treatment of malicious and unavailable evidence links.

evidence.exact_quote: - Review records preserve scope refs, effective reviewer identity, findings, verdict, decision, evidence links, and timestamps.

items.impact: Self-approval, forged evidence, cross-scope decisions, or sensitive evidence exposure can produce an apparently valid promotion.
items.builder_discretion: Define role and scope authorization, separation of duties, evidence integrity and access checks, safe-link handling, and audit redaction.

items.title: Promotion gate facts remain distinct from aggregate state
items.statement: OP-010 explicitly preserves gate facts separately from generic promotion state and requires review scope, identity, findings, verdict, decision, evidence, and timestamps.

evidence.exact_quote: - Promotion gate facts remain separate from generic promotion state.
- Review records preserve scope refs, effective reviewer identity, findings, verdict, decision, evidence links, and timestamps.

items.title: The 13-widget catalog is asserted but not enumerated or falsifiable here
items.statement: OP-011 requires all 13 widget IDs and drill destinations, but the authoritative unit does not enumerate the 13-member set or a machine-checkable catalog reference. The preserved tokens show only three widget IDs plus the host ID.

evidence.exact_quote: Widget-composed Orchestrator content is restricted to Progress, and the 13-widget Progress catalog, drill mappings, labels, action labels, alert taxonomy, event taxonomy, and condition-aging behavior are preserved.
- The progress catalog preserves all 13 widget IDs and drill destinations.

items.impact: A build can omit, duplicate, or misroute widgets and still claim textual conformance.
items.builder_discretion: Provide the canonical 13-entry catalog with IDs, destinations, labels, actions, states, and a completeness validator.

items.title: Progress-only host migration and user experience are undefined
items.statement: Restricting widget composition to Progress has no migration behavior for saved layouts or deep links from former hosts, and no responsive, keyboard, screen-reader, localization, offline, loading, empty, overflow, or large-data requirements.

evidence.exact_quote: - Only Progress remains widget-composed inside Orchestrator.
- Progress state/action/alert/event taxonomies transfer with the catalog.

items.impact: Existing routes or preferences can break, while transferred widgets can be inaccessible, misleading during disconnection, or unusable at scale.
items.builder_discretion: Define compatibility redirects and preference migration plus responsive, accessible, localized, bounded-data, loading, empty, and offline states.

items.title: Transferred widget actions and taxonomy lack transition and authority rules
items.statement: The catalog transfers state, action, alert, and event taxonomies but does not define legal state transitions, action preconditions, caller permissions, duplicate events, action failure, retry, or recovery from a partially completed action.

evidence.exact_quote: - Progress state/action/alert/event taxonomies transfer with the catalog.

items.impact: Widget controls can offer unauthorized or invalid actions and misreport state after failure or retry.
items.builder_discretion: Define a transition table, permissions, idempotency, in-flight state, error truth, and recovery per action.

items.title: External receipts and mutable targets have no trust boundary
items.statement: OP-012 routes external receipts and mutable-target ownership but does not require receipt authenticity, schema/version validation, project binding, replay protection, caller authorization, or an atomic ownership/readiness lease before mutation.

evidence.exact_quote: Artifact routing, external receipts, blocked cards, mutable target ownership, terminal-state precedence, and domain blocked payloads route to owner surfaces with retained lineage and explicit missing-link states.

items.impact: Forged, replayed, cross-project, or stale receipts can route or authorize mutation against the wrong external target.
items.builder_discretion: Specify signed or otherwise authenticated receipts, schema/version checks, scope binding, replay protection, actor permissions, and atomic ownership/readiness preconditions.

items.title: Terminal precedence and missing-link recovery are unspecified
items.statement: The unit names terminal-state precedence and explicit missing-link states but never orders local, publish, remote, timeout, cancellation, and indeterminate outcomes or defines how a missing link is reacquired, reconciled, or retired after network loss.

evidence.exact_quote: Artifact routing, external receipts, blocked cards, mutable target ownership, terminal-state precedence, and domain blocked payloads route to owner surfaces with retained lineage and explicit missing-link states.
- Blocked cards expose publish-capable chains, missing-link explanations, and owner-surface pivots.

items.impact: A UI can present success while the remote outcome is unknown, or remain blocked forever after a recoverable link failure.
items.builder_discretion: Define a precedence table, indeterminate outcome, reconciliation probes, retry/backoff, manual recovery, and terminal retirement rules.

items.title: Replay from last known good is an unconstrained destructive action
items.statement: The preserved replay action has no definition of replay scope, side effects, affected mutable targets, confirmation, authorization, idempotency, cancellation, rollback, or conflict behavior when newer work exists.

evidence.exact_quote: - "Replay from last known good"

items.impact: Replay can duplicate external effects, overwrite newer state, or propagate an old artifact without a safe undo path.
items.builder_discretion: Define authorization, dry-run/impact preview, conflict detection, confirmation, idempotency key, cancellation boundary, and compensating recovery.

items.title: Missing lineage and stale readiness must remain visible and non-dispatchable
items.statement: OP-012 explicitly forbids inventing downstream lineage and forbids Actions-dependent dispatch from stale readiness snapshots.

evidence.exact_quote: - "Do not omit missing downstream links or invent lineage."
- "Do not dispatch Actions-dependent steps from stale readiness snapshots."

items.title: All seven units declare no dependencies despite explicit external seams
items.statement: OP-006 through OP-012 each use empty depends_on arrays although their contracts depend on projection storage, routing, notification consumers, account history, review evidence, widget catalogs, and external SCM/Actions/container systems. No callers, producers, or downstream consumers are bound.

evidence.exact_quote: depends_on: []
depends_on: []
depends_on: []
depends_on: []
depends_on: []
depends_on: []
depends_on: []

items.impact: Compilation and change analysis cannot ensure required producers and consumers implement compatible contracts.
items.builder_discretion: Bind each unit to concrete producer, consumer, owner, and schema/state-machine PlanUnits with versioned seam contracts.

items.title: Validation surfaces cannot falsify runtime or GUI behavior
items.statement: Every unit lists only migration and plan-index validation. Those structural validators cannot demonstrate atomic revalidation, routing isolation, notification ordering, account reconciliation, promotion revocation, catalog completeness, accessible GUI truth, receipt authenticity, or recovery behavior.

evidence.exact_quote: - python3 scripts/pm-plan-migration.py validate --run-dir Plans/.plan_migration/pds-20260611-002-atomize-planunits
- python3 scripts/pm-plan-migration.py validate --run-dir Plans/.plan_migration/pds-20260611-002-atomize-planunits
- python3 scripts/pm-plan-migration.py validate --run-dir Plans/.plan_migration/pds-20260611-002-atomize-planunits
- python3 scripts/pm-plan-migration.py validate --run-dir Plans/.plan_migration/pds-20260611-002-atomize-planunits
- python3 scripts/pm-plan-migration.py validate --run-dir Plans/.plan_migration/pds-20260611-002-atomize-planunits
- python3 scripts/pm-plan-migration.py validate --run-dir Plans/.plan_migration/pds-20260611-002-atomize-planunits
- python3 scripts/pm-plan-migration.py validate --run-dir Plans/.plan_migration/pds-20260611-002-atomize-planunits

items.impact: The units can be declared validated without executing their safety, failure, authority, or GUI contracts.
items.builder_discretion: Add deterministic contract, state-machine, race, fault-injection, authorization, accessibility, localization, migration, and end-to-end oracles with retained diagnostic receipts.

items.title: Cross-unit clock and ordering authority is unknown
items.statement: The window uses last_observed_at, persistence, chronological history, timestamps, condition aging, timeout classes, and remote receipts without naming an authoritative clock, monotonic sequence, skew policy, or ordering fallback. It is unknown whether another contract supplies these invariants.

evidence.exact_quote: - Mutation-capable projections carry projection_state, last_observed_at, source_event_ref, and revalidation_route.
- Review records preserve scope refs, effective reviewer identity, findings, verdict, decision, evidence links, and timestamps.

Widget-composed Orchestrator content is restricted to Progress, and the 13-widget Progress catalog, drill mappings, labels, action labels, alert taxonomy, event taxonomy, and condition-aging behavior are preserved.

items.impact: Clock skew and out-of-order events may corrupt freshness, escalation, history, review order, aging, or terminal precedence.
items.builder_discretion: Resolve whether a canonical time/order contract exists; otherwise define monotonic sequencing, skew tolerance, and deterministic ties.

dimension_assessments.summary: No concrete producers, callers, or consumers are bound for the seven units.
Projection, focus, escalation, account switching, promotion, widget, and receipt transitions are incomplete.
Revalidation, focus routing, owner selection, account history, and mutable target ownership lack race-safe binding.
Storage, history, review, widget actions, and external publication have no complete partial-failure semantics.
Missing receipts, promotion revocation, widget actions, indeterminate remote outcomes, and replay lack bounded recovery.
Route resolution, notification ownership, durable records, reviews, widget actions, and external receipts lack complete actor authority.
Projection lineage, account history, review evidence, and external receipts have no complete retention, redaction, or deletion policy.
Deep links, evidence links, external receipts, blocker payloads, and replay inputs lack validation and authenticity requirements.
Two units with user-visible freshness disclosures are marked non-GUI, and several asynchronous states lack honest in-flight or indeterminate display rules.
Wait recovery, route resolution, widgets, and external publication do not define disconnected or reconnect behavior.
Notification history, widget data, receipt chains, and lineage have no bounds, pagination, backpressure, or overflow rules.
Severity badges, palette routing, timeout cards, and the 13-widget surface lack keyboard, focus, semantic, announcement, and non-color requirements.
Severity, timeout, condition-aging, labels, action labels, timestamps, and history copy have no locale contract.
Stable routes, durable records, evidence, and Progress-only widget hosting lack version and migration behavior.
No runtime diagnostics or retained executable receipts are required for the identified races, failures, or authorization decisions.
Replay, revocation, reopen, and mutable-target operations lack confirmation, impact preview, cancellation, and compensating recovery.
The empty dependency metadata does not bind storage, runtime, routing, review, catalog, or external-system contracts.
The catalog is not fully enumerated and all validation surfaces are structural rather than executable behavioral oracles.
A canonical clock, monotonic ordering, and skew policy may exist elsewhere, but none is visible in the sealed window.
